terms.comment: Greek τὰ ἐπιφάνια, the manifestation; the feast of 6 January in both churches. The West keeps above all the coming of the Magi; the Greek and Slavonic churches keep the Baptism of Christ in the Jordan, with the Great Blessing of the Waters, and call the feast Theophany (τὰ Θεοφάνια).
The feminine singular of Prudentius’s hymn title and of Morgan–Owens.

phrases.latin: vīdēre quod postquam magī, Ēōa prōmunt mūnera, strātīque vōtīs offerunt tūs, myrrham et aurum rēgium
phrases.english: when the Magi saw it, they brought out their gifts from the East and, kneeling in prayer, offered frankincense, myrrh and royal gold

sources: Morgan–Owens, Adumbratio: s.v. Christian: Christmas: Epiphany.
Quotations from the Latinitas loci collections (loci-prudentius), checked against the editions named there.
